takeaways: KKR made $1.78 of adjusted net income per share vs $1.58 expected. Adjusted net income was $1.6 billion, up 29% from a year ago (24/7 Wall St.).

Fee related earnings, the steady, recurring part, hit a record $1.3 billion, up 27%, with management fees of $1.20 billion. Co-CEOs Joe Bae and Scott Nuttall called it a second straight quarter of records.

Not everything shone: total revenue fell 16.5% y/y on lower insurance premiums and investment losses at Global Atlantic, and GAAP EPS of $1.19 included a $230 million impairment. (Revenue "estimates" for KKR are all over the place, so we are not scoring revenue.)

KKR expects to return more than $40 billion to clients in 2026, over 50% above its prior annual record, and the pending sale of USI Insurance should add about $2 billion (over $2.00 a share) of adjusted net income when it closes in Q4.
The board added $500 million to the buyback on Nov 6, leaving $533 million available.
verdict: KKR beat by 20 cents on record fees and is about to hand clients a record $40 billion. Private equity is finally cashing out, which is the part investors actually wanted. The stock fell into the print, so the bar was low. Max respects a firm that returns money.
